props.gloss_en: those who travel through deserts [must give thanks]
one who was ill and recovered [must give thanks]
one who was imprisoned and went free [must give thanks]

whence seafarers? 'they who go down to the sea in ships... they saw the works of the Lord' (Ps 107:23-24), and the storm, their reeling, their crying to the Lord, the calm, their gladness, and 'let them thank the Lord for His kindness' (107:25-31)

whence desert travellers? 'they wandered in the wilderness, in a desolate way, they found no inhabited city... they cried to the Lord... He led them on a straight way... let them thank the Lord for His kindness' (Ps 107:4-8)

one who was ill and recovered: 'fools, because of their transgression... their soul abhorred all food... they cried to the Lord... He sent His word and healed them... let them thank the Lord for His kindness' (Ps 107:17-21)

whence one imprisoned? 'those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death... because they rebelled against the words of God', and 'He humbled their heart with toil', 'they cried to the Lord', 'He brought them out of darkness', 'let them thank the Lord for His kindness' (Ps 107:10-15)
what does he bless? Rav Yehuda: 'Blessed ... who bestows good kindnesses'
Abaye: and he must give thanks before ten
Abaye's source: 'let them exalt Him in the congregation of the people' (Ps 107:32)
Mar Zutra: and two of them [the ten] Sages
Mar Zutra's source: 'and praise Him in the seat of the elders' (Ps 107:32)
the visitors to Rav Yehuda: 'Blessed is the Merciful One who gave you to us and did not give you to the dust'
Rav Yehuda, recovered from illness, to his visitors: you have exempted me from giving thanks
